Divergence 1.5.1 (78)

  • Divergence has a light mode. Open Settings and choose General → Appearance: System, Light or Dark. It is set to System, so unless your Mac is set to Light you will not see any change — Divergence looks exactly as it did.
  • System keeps up with your Mac. If your Mac switches between Light and Dark on its own at sunset, Divergence switches with it while it is open. No restart, and the Settings window changes along with everything else.
  • In Light, each machine tile carries a tint for its platform, and the status colours — “Not encrypted yet”, reachability, latency — were re-tuned so they stay readable against the lighter background.

Divergence 1.5.1 (77)

  • PCs on your network now show under “On this network”. A Windows PC never appeared there, however local it was, because the section was really listing Mac-discovered machines. It now lists machines addressed on your own network, whichever kind they are.
  • Saved connections are separate again, and Remove sticks. If you saved the same machine more than once, those entries were being merged into a single tile — so removing it deleted one entry and the tile came back under another name. You may now see more tiles than before: one per saved connection. That is deliberate, and it is what lets you remove each one individually.
  • Pairing no longer creates a duplicate “Paired Mac” tile, and existing duplicates are merged on first launch (your device list is backed up first).

Divergence 1.5.1 (74)

  • Device status numbers work again. CPU, memory, uptime and battery on the device cards have been blank since late August — a security setting was removed from the app as unused when it was in fact required for status reporting. Restored.
  • Nothing else in this build changes how a session looks or behaves.
